problem:
The value of a savings account $A=A(t)$ after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=kA,
$$

where $k>0$ is the growth rate. If the account initially had $$12\,000,$ and $A(4)=$15\,000,$ calculate the growth rate $k$ to the nearest percent.
worked_solution:
We model the value of the savings account using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=kA.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
A(t)={A}_{0}\,{e}^{kt},
$$

where ${A}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that the account initially had $$12\,000,$ so we have ${A}_{0}=12\,000.$

Therefore, the value $A$ at time $t$ is

$$
A(t)=12\,000\,{e}^{kt}.
$$

Finally, to find the value of $k,$ we substitute $A(4)=15\,000$ into the equation above and solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A(4) & =12\,000\,{e}^{k\cdot 4} \\ 15\,000 & =12\,000\,{e}^{4k} \\ {e}^{4k} & =\frac{15\,000}{12\,000} \\ {e}^{4k} & =1.25 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4k}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ 4k & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.25) \\ k & =0.055\,78…\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k≈6%,$ rounded to the nearest percent.
